issues.legal_issue: A High Court retains jurisdiction to consider extending the time for furnishing security for costs in an appeal to the Supreme Court after a certificate has been granted.
material_facts: The High Court granted a certificate for an appeal to the Supreme Court.
The appellants did not furnish the required security and printing costs by the due date and applied to the High Court to have the late tender accepted.
The High Court rejected the application on the ground that it lacked jurisdiction and cancelled the certificate.
The Supreme Court did not decide whether the appellants had sufficient grounds for condoning the delay.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had jurisdiction to consider the application for an extension. The Supreme Court set aside its order and remitted the application for decision in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Order 45, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, read with the other relevant rules in that Order, does not remove the High Court’s pre-existing jurisdiction to extend time for furnishing security for sufficient cause. The absence in Order 45 of a specified consequence for default under rule 7, contrasted with the express consequence under rule 11 for default under rule 10, supports the view that the court may decide whether to condone the default. Order 12, rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1950 expressly permits the High Court, when security or a deposit is not furnished, to make a further or other order that justice requires, including allowing further time. Section 112 of the Code preserves the operation of Supreme Court rules. The Court followed the approach in Burjore and Bhawani Pershad and approved the cited High Court decisions recognizing jurisdiction, while disapproving Raja Kumar Govind Narayan Singh and Akimuddin Chowdhury.

predicates.certified_supreme_court_appeal: The proceeding is an intended appeal to the Supreme Court for which the High Court has granted a certificate.
predicates.security_not_furnished_on_time: The appellant has not furnished the required security by the applicable deadline.
predicates.extension_application_made: The appellant has applied to the High Court to accept the security after the deadline or allow further time.

issues.definition: When a certified appeal to the Supreme Court involves security not furnished on time and an application for more time, the High Court may consider extending the time.
